messages.subject_clean: [poppr] Creating dendrograms with aboot function from distance matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi Zhian and all,

I got a small issue with the dendrogram drawn using Nei's genetic distance. Hence, thought to include my question in this conversation.

I have to change the font size (population names, nodes values and scale bar) and the position of the scale bar in the dendrogram. I used the tutorial "Population genetics and genomic in R" as my guidance. I drew two dendrograms (Image 1 and 2 attached). I was able to change the font size of the nodes and the position of the scale bar in image two but population names disappeared.
I used following functions.

Image 1

set.seed(999)
tree <- genchar %>%
  genind2genpop(pop = ~field/location()) %>%
  aboot(cutoff = 50, quiet = TRUE, sample = 1000, distance = nei.dist, tree = "upgma")

Image 2

library("ape")
cols <- rainbow(7)
plot.phylo(tree, cex = 0.8, font = 2, adj = 0, tip.color = cols[tree$grp],
           label.offset = 0.0125)
nodelabels(tree$node.label, adj = c(1.3, -0.2), frame = "n", cex = 0.6,
           font = 3, xpd = TRUE)
axisPhylo(1)

 I would be grateful, if you could assist.

Thank you :)

Regards
Buddhika

messages.subject: Uncorrected vs Clone Corrected LD analysis
messages.subject_clean: Uncorrected vs Clone Corrected LD analysis
messages.body_plain:
I work on European populations of a fungal pathogen of apples. Haploid organism. Twelve SSR markers.
I use the linkage disequilibrium analysis in poppr, as you suggest in the tutorial, comparing the non-corrected and clone corrected dataset. I get the following:

... No LD in the uncorrected dataset -> probable sexual reproduction/genetic exchange. Corrected dataset: No LD (p-value = 1; how come?), however the observed association index is off the resampling distribution - I would rather expect a p-value towards 0.05 (in any case lower than in the uncorrected dataset). Or is it because the resampling distribution of the corrected dataset has more variance (approx. -0.05 to +0.05)? Disregarding the p-value how can I interpret the fact that the uncorrected dataset does show evidence for regular genetic exchange and the corrected dataset shows a slight tendency for linkage (however, statistically not significant). So thats kind of the opposite of the example with the North American Phytopthora isolates in your tutorial. Or is that some sort of artefact of my markers/the analysis
Best,
Lukas

messages.subject: Re: could not read the genalex file
messages.subject_clean: could not read the genalex file
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

An "invalid multibyte string" error means that the encoding of your data is not matched with the encoding on your computer. There is a StackOverflow answer for this: https://stackoverflow.com/q/14363085/2752888

I might suggest to try converting your file using read_utf8() and write_utf8() in the {xfun} package to convert your file before reading it into poppr.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm afraid I cannot diagnose this error. There are several reasons why this may be happening. One of the most common problems is if you are loading a previous session and attempt to update a package that is loaded. To prevent that, try following the instructions here to set up your RStudio and R session to avoid reloading your previous working session: https://r4epis.netlify.app/welcome/#configuring-rstudio

Best,

Zhian

Hello,

The cols vector only contains colors, so subsetting it with tree$grp will give no colors. You should add your population names to the cols vector like:

names(cols) <- setPop(genchar, ~field/location) %>% popNames()

Otherwise, I would go through the examples in the plot.phylo function from the {ape} package. It has some good examples.

Best,

Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Uncorrected vs Clone Corrected LD analysis
messages.subject_clean: [poppr] Uncorrected vs Clone Corrected LD analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

The alternative hypothesis for rd is that the correlation between loci is greater than random, so both of those tests fail to reject the null hypothesis.

However, my dissertation research (https://ir.library.oregonstate.edu/concern/graduate_thesis_or_dissertations/dz010t67t?locale=en) showed that significantly negative values of rd can occur in a clonal population when there is low allelic diversity among loci (see section 4.3: https://osf.io/mg82y/). I don't know what your data looks like, so I cannot make any conclusions, but I suspect that may be what's happening.

Best,

Zhian

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Those are functions that are internal to poppr and not for use outside of it. That being said, ia already returns the data frame of the sampled data by using the valuereturn = TRUE argument: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/ia.html#if-there-is-sampling-and-valureturn-true

You can use the raw data from that to customize the plot in any way you see fit. You can define a custom plot function to plot this data from there.

Best,

Zhian

messages.body_snippet: Hi, I'm new to poppr and R in general, I'm doing population analysis for a haploid pathogen. I'm trying to convert the VCF file that I have to genlight object, but for some reason I have got a warning

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] vcfR2genlight object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Noor,

The rule of thumb I'm familiar with is that "Warnings" can be ignored if you understand them. Here you're getting a warning because your data includes loci that have more than two alleles (over your entire sample). The GENLIGHT object was not designed to handle this so they are omitted. I generally ignore this because I typically have a large proportion of loci that only have two alleles so this omission has a minor effect, if any, on the analysis. You appear to have more loci with > 2 alleles than with just 2 alleles which I would consider unusual. That may be because I tend to work on populations of one species. Are you analysing multiple species? Also, you appear to have 98.8% missing data. I think you should look into that because you might not have much to analyze.

I do not feel that there is any "best" object. Different packages written by different authors at different points in time who were working on data in different formats created different objects. I'd call it more of a "different strokes for different folks" matter. We've tried to create conversion tools to help with this. But if you want to work in poppr or adegenet, you'll probably need an object defined in the package. If you want to use ape you'll probably need an object defined in ape.

Good luck!
Brian

messages.body_plain:
Hi Noor,

I think you will find that if you consult the VCF specification

http://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/

you will find that periods (".") are missing data and are not homozygous positions. And if you're working with a haploid organism, you should not have homozygous and heterozygous positions. Each sample should have a single allele called for each variable position. It Sounds to me like you need to figure out whether this is a valid VCF file and whether the genotypes have been correctly called as haploid.

Good luck!
Brian

On Wed, Jul 22, 2020 at 3:14 PM Brian Knaus <brian...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Noor,
>
> The rule of thumb I'm familiar with is that "Warnings" can be ignored if you understand them. Here you're getting a warning because your data includes loci that have more than two alleles (over your entire sample). The GENLIGHT object was not designed to handle this so they are omitted. I generally ignore this because I typically have a large proportion of loci that only have two alleles so this omission has a minor effect, if any, on the analysis. You appear to have more loci with > 2 alleles than with just 2 alleles which I would consider unusual. That may be because I tend to work on populations of one species. Are you analysing multiple species? Also, you appear to have 98.8% missing data. I think you should look into that because you might not have much to analyze.
>
> I do not feel that there is any "best" object. Different packages written by different authors at different points in time who were working on data in different formats created different objects. I'd call it more of a "different strokes for different folks" matter. We've tried to create conversion tools to help with this. But if you want to work in poppr or adegenet, you'll probably need an object defined in the package. If you want to use ape you'll probably need an object defined in ape.
>
> Good luck!
> Brian
